summary: This entry has absorbed the D-089 findings — the lead target is unique, the condition-2 block preserves both prior remainders and adds its own, and the block is fenced. The eligibility case is the strongest of the three re-records: D-008 says in terms that only the evidence is slice-scoped and that each future role's closure evidence sits at its own DR-G14 qualification, so future-role closures are routed rather than silently closed. Two citation defects remain. The lead-prefix target is quoted in a backtick span but itself contains backticks, which is D089-SF-1 recurring at the one target that now carries inner backticks and did not at D-089 — the fence was applied to the block that needed it last time, not to the string that needs it this time. And the recitation quotes DR-G14's recorded identifier as `harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux` when file 08 records `harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux.typescript`; the dropped suffix is precisely the role-scoping the gate-2 argument rests on.

objections.location: Subject, Decision clause 4, first bullet: the lead-prefix target and its replacement
objections.claim: The lead-prefix target is delimited by backticks but contains backticks, so the byte-exact specification does not unambiguously state the string to match or the string to write.
objections.why: The target reads `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED** — rule ACCEPTED universally (`COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md` D-008, CONSENT `cd08c5f0…`);` and the replacement mirrors it. Both carry two inner backtick spans, each of which closes the enclosing span, so an executor copying the text between the outer delimiters gets a truncated string. This is the same defect I raised at D-089 as D089-SF-1 and that was repaired there by fencing, which makes its reappearance worth stating precisely: at D-089 the inner backticks were in the condition-2 block and the lead prefix had none, so fencing the block was sufficient. Here the situation is inverted — the condition-2 block is correctly fenced, and the inner backticks have moved into the lead prefix, which is not. The remedy was applied to the location that needed it last time rather than to the string that needs it this time. It matters more here than it did at D-089 because this is the replacement that records SATISFIED, and because I could only confirm the target's uniqueness by reconstructing the full string including its inner backticks from the live cell — the draft alone does not determine it. The intent is recoverable from the live DR-119 status cell, which is why this is not a MUST-FIX.
objections.repair: Put the lead-prefix target and its replacement in fenced blocks, as clause 4's third bullet already does, or escape the inner backticks as D-085 did.

objections.location: Subject, Eligibility recitation item 3: "after D-088 carries a recorded identifier `harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux`"
objections.claim: The recorded identifier is misquoted. File 08 records `harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux.typescript`; the entry drops the `.typescript` suffix while presenting the string as the recorded identifier.
objections.why: I read the DR-G14 harness cell rather than trusting the quotation, and it reads 'named: harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux.typescript (D-086; not authored; not QUALIFIED).' The string the entry quotes exists in file 08 only as a prefix of the real identifier, never as a complete one — an occurrence count returns one for each, because the shorter is a substring of the longer. That is the shape of citation error this corpus is least tolerant of, and the dropped element is not incidental. The whole of gate 2 turns on the evidence being scoped to the current slice-1 role: the recitation says 'Evidence is slice-scoped (TypeScript now)', the decision says 'TypeScript-role closure evidence remains condition 4 / DR-G14', and D-008 says each future role's evidence sits 'at its own DR-G14 qualification'. The `.typescript` suffix is exactly how file 08 records that role scoping on the named harness. Quoting the identifier without it removes the one piece of the register that corroborates the entry's central argument, and it does so inside backticks, which in this corpus reads as a verbatim citation. Gate 3 itself still holds — DR-G14 exists, has an owner and carries a recorded identifier — which is why this is not a MUST-FIX.

notesNonBlocking.location: Subject, Eligibility recitation item 2: 'Authoring of a later language role's closure, and DR-120 packager/adapter design, remain other rows' work'
notesNonBlocking.observation: The sentence bundles two leftovers that live in different places, and it is accurate for only one of them. DR-120 packager/adapter design is genuinely another row, and I confirmed DR-120 is live in file 08 with an OPEN lead. A later language role's closure is not another row's work: D-008 places it on this same rule and this same gate, 'each future role's closure evidence at its own DR-G14 qualification', which is condition-4 work at DR-G14 deferred to that role's own qualification. The conclusion the sentence draws — that neither is this row's remaining acceptance-evidence member — is right either way, and the entry names the correct destination two sentences later at 'remain condition 4 / DR-G14'. Splitting the sentence so each leftover names its own destination would remove the imprecision.

The attack 'lead replacement is not unique' fails, and the D-089 lesson is visibly applied. The target string, reconstructed in full including its inner backticks, occurs exactly once in the live register, while the bare `**DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED**` token occurs four times — matching the entry's own rejected alternative 'Replace the bare four-occurrence lead token. Rejected: D089-MF-1 class.' The four are the residue after DR-115 flipped, so the count is independently consistent with the register's history.

The attack 'leftover is not only qualification' fails, and D-008's own bytes are why rather than the entry's characterisation of them. D-008 records the rule as 'ACCEPTED UNIVERSALLY — it binds EVERY supported language role, per the row's own unconditional quantifier (turn-1 MF: the draft's per-role re-acceptance hook is struck); only the EVIDENCE is slice-scoped (TypeScript now, each future role's closure evidence at its own DR-G14 qualification).' Both halves of the entry's claim — that per-role re-acceptance was struck and that only evidence is slice-scoped — are verbatim from the adopted decision, and future-role closures are explicitly routed to a later DR-G14 qualification rather than silently closed.

The attack 'D-085 / D-089 remainders dropped from the snapshot' fails, established by fragment-by-fragment comparison of the live condition-2 cell against the proposed block rather than by reading the new text for plausibility. Every sentence of the live cell appears verbatim in the replacement — DR-102's 'leftover CC-1..CC-11 execution remains at DR-G21 / condition 4', DR-115's 'leftover measurement remains at DR-G01..G05 / condition 4', and DR-103's accepted-contract note — with the sole exception of the counts sentence, whose change is the point of the edit. The block adds DR-119's own 'leftover TypeScript-role closure evidence remains at DR-G14 / condition 4', so all three satisfied rows now name a remainder.

The counts verify against my own tally rather than either cell's assertion. The live lead-label tally over the thirty DR-1xx rows is 22 OPEN, 2 SATISFIED, 4 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, summing to thirty, with DR-119 leading DECIDED. Flipping DR-119 gives exactly the entry's 3, 22, 3 and 2, again summing to thirty. The clause 'condition 2 remains 2 of 30 SATISFIED' is present verbatim and exactly once, so the attack 'stale 2 of 30 after C2 becomes 3 of 30' fails.

The attack 'leaves Blueprint-impact hard-blocker' fails. The target 'Hard blocker for every supported language role; TypeScript specifically must not require user-managed Node' is verbatim and unique, and the replacement displaces the hard-blocker while preserving both honest residues — 'The universal D-008 rule stands. Not QUALIFIED.' That the universal rule is preserved matters here in a way it did not for DR-102 or DR-115, because D-008's rule binds every role and only the evidence was slice-scoped; dropping it would have narrowed an adopted universal rule by a file-08 edit.

The attack 'applies the split to DR-120 or DR-118' fails. Clause 5 refuses DR-103/118/123 and the rejected alternative 'Mark DR-120 SATISFIED. Rejected: no T2-02 contract; packager authoring remains design' is apt on two independent grounds I checked: DR-120's live lead is OPEN, so Class B's DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED trigger does not apply to it either, and D-056's Class A route needs a T2-02 contract it does not have.

The attack 'treats G14 execution as architecture SATISFIED' fails: clause 2 states the closure evidence 'is not architecture SATISFIED evidence and is not an architecture hard blocker', clause 5 adds 'Does not author a TypeScript runtime closure', and the header refuses to execute DR-G14.
The attack 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fails: both occurrences are refusals, the rejected alternative survives, and the readiness effect keeps condition 5 NOT MET and last.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on every row, and nothing moved under the entry: COORD 4846d9d2…, file 08 36ecbea8… and the freeze all match at the start and again at the end of this review. The commits resolve at full hash — 75c981dd… to D-056, acdfaed5… to the D-089 writer that touched file 08, and 7ddbbca4… to 'D-090: remove duplicate D-089 heading'. D-008's CONSENT digest cd08c5f0… is present in COORD.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and two SHOULD-FIX. This is the best-prepared of the three SATISFIED re-records — the lead target is unique on its own, both prior rows' remainders survive the snapshot rewrite, its own remainder is added, and the condition-2 block is fenced. The eligibility case is also the cleanest, because D-008 anticipated the exact question gate 2 asks and answered it in its own text: the rule binds every role, only the evidence is slice-scoped, and each future role's evidence sits at its own DR-G14 qualification. Both objections are citation defects rather than reasoning defects. The first is D089-SF-1 reappearing at a different target: the fence went to the condition-2 block, which is where the inner backticks were last time, while this time they are in the lead prefix, which is the string that records SATISFIED and the one I had to reconstruct from the live cell to test at all. The second is a truncated identifier — file 08 records harness.DR-G14.language-runtime-ux.typescript and the entry quotes it without the role suffix, which is the single element of the register that corroborates the slice-scoping the whole gate-2 argument depends on. Both repairs are mechanical and neither touches the eligibility case.
